tweet_summary: An engagement-poll post about removing Pete Hegseth shows a graphic claiming '🚨 NEW POLL: 75% of Americans say Pete Hegseth should be removed from office.'
why_note_decision: The '75%' figure in the graphic is fabricated — no credible poll shows 75% of Americans wanting Hegseth removed. The real, identifiable poll on this question is a J.L. Partners/Daily Mail survey (Mar 25-27, 1,001 registered voters) showing 54% backing his resignation and 22% saying he should stay. The graphic inflates that to a fake '75% of Americans / removed from office' statistic with a 'NEW POLL' siren framing, which is a checkable false numerical claim being spread as fact. A note correcting the fabricated number is warranted. Provisional 'no_note' is wrong.
judge_guidance: A correct note must establish that the '75% of Americans say Hegseth should be removed' statistic is fabricated/unsupported, and should cite the real figure: a J.L. Partners/Daily Mail poll found ~54% support his resignation and ~22% say he should stay. PASS if the note flags '75%' as unsupported AND supplies the actual poll numbers with a reliable source (The Hill / Newsweek / Daily Mail-J.L. Partners). FAIL if it (a) merely opines on Hegseth, (b) says 'no note needed', or (c) repeats the 75% figure. The original note had the right correction but cite-quality/relevance dragged it down, so a correct note must cleanly tie the real 54% poll to the fake 75% graphic.
reference_note: The '75%' figure is fabricated; no credible poll shows 75% of Americans want Hegseth removed. The actual poll on this question, by J.L. Partners/Daily Mail (Mar 25-27, 1,001 registered voters), found 54% support his resignation and 22% say he should stay. https://thehill.com/policy/defense/5220560-hegseth-resign-poll-waltz-vance-signalgate-atlantic-goldberg

original_unhelpful_note.text: The graphic depicts a fabricated poll; no credible survey shows 75% of Americans want Pete Hegseth removed from office. A J.L. Partners/Daily Mail poll found 54% of voters support his resignation. https://thehill.com/policy/defense/5220560-hegseth-resign-poll-waltz-vance-signalgate-atlantic-goldberg https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/mar/31/pete-hegseth-republican-voters
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substance is correct (75% fabricated; real poll 54% resign) but rated notHelpfulIncorrect(3)/OpinionSpeculation(2)/Argumentative(2). Low rating volume (6); calling it 'fabricated' without showing the graphic is literally a fake number vs a misreported real poll may have read as overreach to some raters. A correct note states the real number plainly and labels 75% unsupported.

fact_check.claim_verdict: False: '75% removed' is fabricated; real J.L. Partners/Daily Mail poll = 54% resign, 22% stay.
fact_check.notes: No poll supports '75% of Americans want Hegseth removed'. J.L. Partners/Daily Mail poll (Mar 25-27, 1,001 registered voters, +/-3.4): 54% back resignation, 22% say stay. A separate viral '75% want him impeached/prosecuted, per CNN' claim is also false (CNN never reported it).

importance.lens_rationale: Fabricated polling numbers distort public perception of opinion on a cabinet official; correcting invented statistics protects the integrity of public-opinion discourse, moderate value.
